beschreibung: How can meaning be measured, and what do we actually know about the effectiveness of meaning-centered interventions? This module presents central measurement instruments of meaning research, conveys basic concepts of intervention research from study designs to effect sizes and meta-analyses, and enables participants to read studies critically and to assess the evidence on logotherapy honestly.
lernziele: You can describe the Purpose in Life Test, the Meaning in Life Questionnaire and the LeBe questionnaire in terms of their basic ideas, strengths and limitations.
You can distinguish common study designs and explain the logic of randomized controlled trials.
You can understand the basics of effect sizes and meta-analyses and qualitatively summarize the central finding of the meta-analysis by Vos et al. (2015).
You can read studies critically on the basis of central quality criteria.
You can name the limits of the evidence on logotherapy and communicate them honestly to clients and professional colleagues.

pruefung.frage: Which two dimensions does the Meaning in Life Questionnaire (Steger et al., 2006) assess?
optionen: Meaningfulness and crisis of meaning
Presence of meaning and search for meaning
Creative and experiential values
Vertical and horizontal self-transcendence
pruefung.erklaerung: The MLQ distinguishes presence of meaning and search for meaning. Meaningfulness and crisis of meaning (A) are scales of the LeBe; self-transcendence dimensions (D) belong to its sources of meaning.

pruefung.aussage: In addition to meaningfulness and crisis of meaning, the LeBe questionnaire also assesses numerous sources of meaning, that is, sources from which people derive meaning.
pruefung.erklaerung: True. The LeBe (Schnell & Becker, 2007) separates the degree of experienced meaning from its sources and assesses 26 sources of meaning in five dimensions.

pruefung.frage: Why does a cross-sectional study that finds an association between experienced meaning and depressiveness not allow the conclusion that meaning protects against depression?
optionen: Because cross-sectional studies are fundamentally unreliable
Because depressiveness cannot be measured
Because associations can never become statistically significant
Because reverse causality or third variables can also explain the association
pruefung.erklaerung: Correlations leave the direction of effect open; reverse causality and third variables are possible explanations (D). The other options are factually wrong.

pruefung.frage: Which features characterize a methodologically sound randomized controlled trial? (Multiple answers possible)
optionen: Random allocation to intervention and control groups
A primary outcome measure specified in advance
Analysis only of those who completed the intervention
Intention-to-treat analysis
Blinded outcome assessment, as far as possible
pruefung.erklaerung: Randomization, preregistration of the primary outcome, intention-to-treat analysis and blinded assessment are quality features. A completers-only analysis (C) can bias the results.

pruefung.frage: What does an effect size of d = 0.8 mean when comparing two groups?
optionen: The difference in means amounts to 0.8 standard deviations; by Cohen’s conventions, a large effect.
80 percent of participants benefited.
The probability of error is 0.8 percent.
The intervention works by 0.8 points for every person.
pruefung.erklaerung: Cohen’s d is a standardized mean difference; according to Cohen, 0.8 is roughly considered large. It is neither a proportion (B) nor a probability of error (C) nor an individual raw score (D).

pruefung.aussage: An advantage over a waiting-list control group demonstrates that the specific elements of an intervention are effective.
pruefung.erklaerung: False. Waiting-list comparisons cannot separate nonspecific factors such as attention and expectation from specific effects. Active control conditions are needed for this.

pruefung.frage: Which statement most accurately reflects the meta-analysis by Vos, Craig and Cooper (2015)?
optionen: All existential therapies showed large, uniform effects.
Existential therapies showed no effects whatsoever.
Structured, meaning-centered interventions showed favorable findings, other existential approaches less clear ones; the body of studies was heterogeneous.
The meta-analysis examined exclusively case studies of classical logotherapy.
pruefung.erklaerung: The meta-analysis pooled RCTs and found the most favorable findings for structured, meaning-centered interventions, with a heterogeneous body of studies (C).

pruefung.frage: Which factors limit the evidence on classical logotherapy? (Multiple answers possible)
optionen: Frequently small samples
Unclear manualization of the interventions
Frequently missing active control conditions
Too many independent replications
Predominantly theory-proximal outcome measures such as the PIL
pruefung.erklaerung: Small samples, unclear manualization, missing active controls and theory-proximal outcome measures limit the informative value. An excess of independent replications (D) is precisely not the problem – on the contrary, they are frequently lacking.
